ACS Energy Letters | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in a chlorination-tailored strategy using SiCl4 to convert rigid [PO4] units into flexible [POxCl4–x] motifs, creating a low-cost, deformable amorphous phosphate-based chloride solid electrolyte. Its significance is enabling high Na+ conductivity (2.02 mS cm–1), low modulus (1.8 GPa), and stable interfacial contact, allowing 4.5 V all-solid-state sodium batteries to cycle over 2000 times at only 5 MPa stack pressure.

item.description:

ACS Energy Letters | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in a semi-single-crystal NCM622 architecture combining ~2 μm single-crystalline primary particles within a conventional ~6–7 μm secondary-particle framework. This bridges the trade-off between polycrystalline and single-crystal cathodes, preserving high electrode density and rate capability while suppressing intergranular cracking and improving cycling stability—without the aggressive pulverization required for conventional single-crystal cathodes.
🏷 NCM cathode · semi-single-crystal · intergranular cracking · lithium-ion battery · cycling stability

Advanced Functional Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in using cockroach digestion of zinc-enriched feed to create surface-porous hard carbon with abundant closed pores, N/S doping, and expanded interlayer spacing (0.43 nm). This biogenic strategy yields exceptional sodium storage: 148.9 mAh g⁻¹ at 32 C and 56.9% retention over 7000 cycles, enabling high-rate full cells. It offers a sustainable, scalable route to advanced SIB anodes.

💡 The novelty lies in flower-like 3D porous ZnO@C scaffolds with tunable lithiophilic loading, linking alloy-phase evolution to pore-filling Li deposition. Operando XRD and DFT reveal LiZn phase-dominated epitaxial growth. Significance: dendrite-free cycling over 1200 h at 37 mV hysteresis, stable LFP/NMC-811 full cells, and a rational structure-phase-deposition design principle for high-energy Li metal batteries.

item.title: Synchronously Regulating Bipolar Interfacial Chemistry for Ultrastable Zn─I 2 Batteries
item.description:

Advanced Functional Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 Trace-level calcium dobesilate enables synchronous bipolar regulation via cation-anion cooperation: D⁻ tunes Zn²⁺ solvation and coordinates I₂, while Ca²⁺/D⁻ co-adsorb to form a hybrid SEI. This suppresses dendrites, side reactions, and polyiodide shuttling, yielding ultrastable Zn||I₂ batteries (4200 h cycling; 92.76% retention after 12,000 cycles), offering a cost-effective, eco-friendly electrolyte design for practical grid storage.

item.description:

💡 The novelty lies in selectively infusing liquid Sn into grain boundaries of a Zn(002) anode, shielding defect-sensitive intergranular regions while preserving deposition-guiding basal domains. Journal of Materials Chemistry A | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in dual-carbon-shielded hollow bimetallic sulfide heterostructures, combining void engineering, heterointerfaces, and carbon protection. This design buffers volume changes, boosts conductivity, and accelerates reaction kinetics, enabling high-capacity, stable, and fast-charging anodes for both lithium- and sodium-ion batteries—advancing high-energy-density TMS-based electrode development.

item.title: Reconciling Pore Closure with Ion Accessibility for High-Rate and Stable Sodium Storage in Hard Carbon

Journal of Materials Chemistry A | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in reconciling pore closure with ion accessibility, revealing that carbon-layer rearrangement creates confined sodium-storage environments whose utility depends on pore accessibility within the current-imposed timescale. This resolves a key trade-off in hard carbon design, enabling high-rate and stable sodium storage and offering mechanistic guidance for optimizing nanopore architecture in sodium-ion battery anodes.
